summary: 14-day CGM data shows 86% TIR with a 5.1% TBR that is concentrated overnight and associated with correction bolus over-corrections. An aggressive dynamic ISF system with UAM and SMB enabled is reacting to a 10-hour DIA that overestimates insulin-on-board, leading to excessive insulin delivery and repeated hypoglycemia. Meal data is absent, blocking carb ratio and bolus strategy evaluation. The primary issue is the DIA mismatch with modern insulin action, which must be corrected before any other profile or automation tuning.

analysis_steps.evidence: CGM coverage 98.7%, 3995 valid entries, 10 gaps up to 65 min, cadence 5 min. No invalid or duplicate entries. Insulin and pump telemetry present.
analysis_steps.findings: Data quality sufficient for all downstream analysis.

analysis_steps.evidence: Overall TBR 5.1%, with 5 days above 5% and Aug 18 at 12.8%. Minimum glucose 41 mg/dL (Aug 14), 42 mg/dL (Aug 13, Aug 21). CV 32.6%.
analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia is the primary safety concern; any future adjustments must avoid worsening lows.

analysis_steps.evidence: Local-time hourly glucose from 00:00–06:00 averages 90–106 mg/dL but with TBR up to 18.5% (01:00). Minimum values of 41–54 mg/dL appear overnight. Basal rates 0.6–0.8 U/h are modest. Multiple correction boluses (e.g., 0.2 U at 02:30) followed by rapid drops suggest excessive IOB accumulation from the 10-h DIA.
analysis_steps.findings: Overnight hypoglycemia appears driven by automation IOB miscalculation rather than basal rate alone. Basal adjustment should wait until DIA is corrected.
data_gaps: No meal logs to separate postprandial IOB
No direct basal testing during fasting periods without correction boluses

analysis_steps.evidence: DIA set to 10 h, modern rapid-acting insulin typically 4-6 h. Therapy response windows show massive glucose drops after small correction doses (e.g., 0.2 U from 234 mg/dL to 56 mg/dL) coinciding with high IOB. ISF 56 mg/dL/U; some over-correction may stem from IOB miscalculation. Carb ratios present but meal data absent.
analysis_steps.findings: 10-hour DIA is the root cause of IOB overestimation, leading to excessive SMB/temp basal delivery and severe hypoglycemia. ISF may need review after DIA correction. CR evaluation is blocked by missing meal logs.
data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries; CR effectiveness cannot be assessed

analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM enabled. Over-correction hypoglycemia (e.g., Aug 14 0.2 U → 56 mg/dL) occurs with UAM-boosted SMBs when IOB is already high. SMB with temp target enabled.
analysis_steps.findings: Automation mechanisms are working as designed but are compounding the DIA-induced IOB error. No need to disable SMB/UAM now.

analysis_steps.evidence: Dynamic ISF enabled (factor 70%), autosens off. sensitivity_ratio remains near 1.0. Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h are not reached. Safety limits not causative.
analysis_steps.findings: Automation sensitivity and safety limits are not the primary driver. Keep all settings; re-evaluate after DIA correction.
data_gaps: Dynamic ISF response after DIA change is uncertain

analysis_steps.findings: No meal entries (carb_treatment_entries=0). Postprandial patterns cannot be separated from UAM/SMB effects. Carb ratio and prebolus timing evaluation impossible.
analysis_steps.evidence: Telemetry shows zero logged carbs and no bolus-wizard records.
data_gaps: All meal data (grams, time, bolus details) missing

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carb entries present. e-carb absorption patterns cannot be analyzed.

analysis_steps.evidence: Cross-referenced all findings: DIA is the root cause of over-aggressive insulin delivery and subsequent hypoglycemia. All other profile settings and automation parameters are safe but their evaluation is confounded by the DIA error. Meal strategy analysis blocked by absent data.
analysis_steps.findings: The single most impactful change is to reduce DIA to 5 h. No other profile or AAPS settings should be adjusted concurrently. After DIA correction and a stable 5-7 day observation, basal rates and ISF can be reassessed. Meal logging must begin to enable future meal strategy tuning.

strengths: Overall TIR of 86% reflects generally good glucose control despite variability.
CGM coverage at 98.7% provides high-quality data for analysis.
Automation (SMB/UAM) is correctly configured and responsive to glucose changes.
A consistent profile structure with multiple time segments enables fine-tuning.
issues: Recurrent hypoglycemia (lowest 41 mg/dL) driven by over-aggressive insulin delivery due to DIA-induced IOB miscalculation.
10-hour DIA is incompatible with modern rapid-acting insulin kinetics, causing the algorithm to underestimate active insulin.
Absent meal logging prevents carb ratio and prebolus optimization.
Overnight TBR elevated to 18.5% in some hours, reflecting unnecessary insulin dosing.

recommendations.title: Reduce Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) to 5 hours
recommendations.description: The current 10 h DIA leads to significant IOB overestimation, driving excessive SMB and temp basal delivery, particularly overnight and after correction boluses. Shortening DIA to 5 h will align IOB calculations with typical rapid-acting insulin action, reducing hypoglycemia risk without impairing hyperglycemia correction.

recommendations.title: Log All Meal Carbohydrates to Enable Future Strategy Tuning
recommendations.description: Missing carbohydrate entries prevent evaluation of carb ratios, prebolus timing, and extended carb strategies. Accurate logging for at least 7 consecutive days is necessary before any meal-related settings can be adjusted.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Change DIA from 10 h to 5 h. Make no other profile changes at the same time.
profile_recommendation.rationale: A 10 h DIA overestimates insulin-on-board with rapid-acting insulin, causing the automation to deliver excess insulin via SMBs and temp basals. This over-delivery is the most plausible explanation for the observed severe hypoglycemia (e.g., 41 mg/dL). A 5 h DIA is well-supported by insulin action data and will immediately reduce unnecessary insulin dosing.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After changing DIA, monitor overnight glucose and post-correction patterns for 5-7 days without altering other settings. If hypoglycemia persists, consider small basal reductions but only after verifying the DIA adjustment effect.

10 h DIA overestimates IOB for rapid-acting insulin, leading to excessive SMB/temp basal delivery. Changing to 5 h aligns IOB with actual insulin action and immediately reduces hypoglycemia risk. Supported by multiple therapy response windows showing massive drops after small corrections.
SMB and UAM are functioning correctly; the hypoglycemia is caused by IOB miscalculation from DIA, not by these features. After DIA correction, their behavior should be safe.
Current activation settings are conservative enough (no SMB with COB or after carbs). SMB with temp target enabled is acceptable; no evidence of misuse.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Start logging all meals (carb grams, timing, and bolus details) to enable future meal strategy. Without logged data, no specific prebolus timing, bolus split, or e-carb recommendation can be made. After DIA correction, the automation will provide basal and SMB coverage, but meal boluses will still require manual entry with accurate carb counts.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Zero carbohydrate entries over 14 days; all meal-related inferences are impossible. Even unlogged meal patterns are corrupted by DIA-induced IOB errors. Logging for at least 7 days is prerequisite for any CR, prebolus, or extended carb evaluation.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log all meal intake (grams and time) alongside glucose and pump data for the next 7 consecutive days, then re-analyze meal patterns.

implementation_steps: 1. Change the profile Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) from 10 h to 5 h. Do not alter any other profile or AAPS settings at this time.
2. Monitor CGM closely for the next 5-7 days, especially overnight (00:00–06:00) and for 4-6 hours after any correction bolus. Note any changes in hypoglycemia frequency and overall TIR.

3. If hypoglycemia persists after DIA correction, consider a small reduction in the overnight basal segments (e.g., 0.05–0.1 U/h) but only after confirming that the DIA change is stable and IOB calculations are accurate.

4. Begin logging all carbohydrate intake (grams, time, and bolus timing) consistently for at least 7 full days. This will enable future evaluation and optimization of carb ratios and prebolus strategies.
5. After basal and meal patterns are stable, review ISF using observed correction doses. If over-correction still occurs, consider a moderate ISF increase (e.g., 60-65 mg/dL/U) as a separate change.
6. Re-evaluate Dynamic ISF and SMB delivery parameters only after the above steps, using updated meal data and IOB accuracy.
education: A Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) that is too long makes the algorithm 'think' insulin is active for many hours, drastically underestimating insulin-on-board (IOB). This leads to additional insulin delivery (SMBs, temp basals) that can cause dangerous hypoglycemia.

Modern rapid-acting insulin analogs (like Fiasp, Humalog, Novolog) typically have a DIA of 4-6 h in most individuals. A 5 h DIA is a safe starting point that more closely matches real-world insulin clearance.
Consistent meal logging (grams, time, bolus) is essential for automated systems to fine-tune carb ratios and timing. Without it, meal-related settings cannot be accurately evaluated.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Do not alter multiple insulin-delivery settings simultaneously. After changing DIA, allow a full 5-7 days of observation before considering any further profile adjustments.
Always discuss significant profile changes with your healthcare provider.
Monitor for unexpected hyperglycemia after DIA reduction. If post-meal highs increase, meal bolus timing and carb ratios may need adjustment, but only after meal logging data is available.
